content: The medication is indicated for the treatment of hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia (HABP) and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (VABP) caused by susceptible isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus complex (ABC). The recommended dosage is 2 grams (1 gram of sulbactam and 1 gram of durlobactam) administered intravenously every 6 hours, infused over 3 hours. The treatment duration is typically 7 to 14 days, but it should be adjusted based on the patient’s clinical status. This medication is not indicated for HABP/VABP caused by pathogens other than susceptible isolates of ABC. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and maintain effectiveness, it should only be used to treat or prevent infections that are proven or strongly suspected to be bacterial in origin. The safety and efficacy of this drug have not been established in all populations. Since the drug is substantially excreted by the kidneys, elderly patients with reduced renal function may require dosage adjustments based on their renal function. Certain drug interactions may increase the plasma concentration of sulbactam/durlobactam, potentially leading to adverse effects. For example: Ceftobiprole, an OATP1B1/1B3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of sulbactam/durlobactam. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin, erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, or stearate forms), and cyclosporine may increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Eluxadoline, enasidenib, encorafenib, fostemsavir, gemfibrozil, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, grapefruit, leniolisib, pazopanib, ritonavir, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, tacrolimus, telmisartan, trofinetide, verapamil, and voxilaprevir may also increase sulbactam/durlobactam levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Sulbactam is predicted to undergo active secretion via OATP1, which is a significant pathway for its clearance. Inhibition of OATP1 may increase sulbactam plasma concentrations, necessitating caution with co-administration of drugs that inhibit this pathway. Additionally, sulbactam/durlobactam may reduce the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors such as atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, cosibelimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, and toripalimab. Co-administration may interfere with the efficacy of these agents, and caution with close monitoring is advised. For patients receiving oral microbiota therapies, sulbactam/durlobactam may decrease their efficacy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is recommended to complete antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy.
